BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

DO $$
BEGIN
  -- Skip entirely once full_name has been dropped (re-run after contract step).
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
             WHERE table_schema = current_schema()
               AND table_name = 'users' AND column_name = 'full_name') THEN

    -- Only touches rows not yet migrated, so re-runs never overwrite later edits.
    UPDATE users
    SET first_name = substring(btrim(full_name) from '^\S+'),
        last_name  = nullif(btrim(substring(btrim(full_name) from '^\S+\s+(.*)$')), '')
    WHERE first_name IS NULL
      AND last_name  IS NULL
      AND nullif(btrim(full_name), '') IS NOT NULL;
  END IF;
END $$;

COMMIT;

Behavior: `"Ada Lovelace"` → `Ada` / `Lovelace`; `"Mary Jane Watson"` → `Mary` / `Jane Watson`; `"Cher"` → `Cher` / `NULL`.

Skipped: batching, since a single `UPDATE` is fine up to a few million rows. For larger tables, loop over id ranges to avoid long locks. Also skipped: dropping `full_name` in the same run, because it's irreversible and the old app version still needs it during rollout. Name-splitting is a heuristic (it won't handle "van der Berg" or single-field mononyms perfectly), so spot-check before dropping the old column.
